subject: Biotechnology
title: Biosensors
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Biosensors.

hook.text: Engineer a cell to glow when it detects arsenic in water — a living sensor for environmental toxins.

buildup.text: Transcription factors that naturally respond to specific chemicals are wired to reporter genes like GFP.

discovery.text: Paper-based biosensors freeze-dry engineered cells onto strips — add a water sample and read the color change.

twist.text: Sensitivity must be tuned — too sensitive and normal concentrations trigger false alarms. Calibration is critical.

climax.text: Wearable biosensors detect cortisol in sweat — synthetic circuits in hydrogels monitor stress in real time.

punchline.text: Living cells as detectors — biosensors turn biology into measurement tools.

quiz.question: How do paper-based biosensors work?
options: They use electronic chips embedded in paper to detect chemicals
Freeze-dried engineered cells on paper rehydrate when a sample is added and produce a visible signal
They absorb the chemical and change color through a purely physical reaction
